# i2 Notebook Web SDK — full documentation bundle

This single file concatenates the agent guide, the complete guide, and the API rollup so a language model can ingest the whole SDK in one fetch. Source of truth: https://i2group.github.io/notebook-sdk/

<!-- BEGIN: Agent guide (AGENTS.md) -->

# AGENTS.md — i2 Notebook Web SDK

Guidance for AI coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc.) writing i2 Analyst's
Notebook **web client plug-ins** with `@i2analyze/notebook-sdk`. Follow this over habits learned
from other SDKs. If a rule here conflicts with a code sample you found online, this file wins.

Docs: https://i2group.github.io/notebook-sdk/ · API reference: https://i2group.github.io/notebook-sdk/api/ · Machine-readable: https://i2group.github.io/notebook-sdk/llms.txt

---

## 0. The one rule that matters most: how to start a plug-in

**To create a NEW plug-in project, ALWAYS scaffold with the tool. Never hand-write a project
skeleton, and never copy a sample or tutorial as the starting boilerplate.**

```sh
npm create @i2analyze/notebook-plugin       # or: npx @i2analyze/create-notebook-plugin
```

Templates (pass `--template=`):

- `plugin` (default) — headless plug-in with an `entrypoint.ts`, no UI.
- `plugin-with-toolview` — adds a React tool view (`ToolView` component + `index.html`).

```sh
npm create @i2analyze/notebook-plugin -- --template=plugin-with-toolview
```

The scaffold wires up TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, webpack production bundling, the dev proxy
(`devproxy.json`), and a correct `plugin.json` manifest. Reproducing this by hand gets the manifest,
CSP, version pinning, and build config subtly wrong.

> ❌ **Do NOT** treat `samples/basic-plugin` or the guide page **"Creating a basic plug-in for the
> i2 Web Client"** (`tutorials/basic-plugin.md`) as the recommended boilerplate. Those exist to
> *explain concepts from first principles*. The recommended path for real plug-ins is the
> **`create-notebook-plugin` tool** and its tutorial (`tutorials/create-notebook-plugin.md`).
> When a user asks you to "make a plug-in", scaffold with the tool, then edit `src/entrypoint.ts`.

If you cannot run the scaffolder (e.g. offline), say so explicitly and reproduce the generated
`plugin/` template structure faithfully rather than inventing a layout.

---

## 1. Mental model

A plug-in is static assets (JS + a `plugin.json` manifest) served to the i2 Web Client. Three parts:

1. **Manifest** (`public/plugin.json`) — identity (`pluginId`, `name`, `pluginVersion`), the
   `entryPointUrl`, and CSP. Schema:
   `https://i2group.github.io/notebook-sdk/schemas/plugin-manifest.json` (keep the `$schema` line —
   it gives editors and agents live validation).
2. **Entry point** (`src/entrypoint.ts`) — runs on load. Acquires the versioned API, registers
   capabilities (commands, tool views), then calls `api.initializationComplete()`.
3. **Tool views** (optional) — iframed HTML/JS UIs (React in the template) for richer interaction.

## 2. Acquiring the API — the version you request is a minimum, not "your SDK version"

```ts
import { NotebookStatic } from '@i2analyze/notebook-sdk';
declare const notebook: NotebookStatic;

async function main() {
  const api = await notebook.getEntryPointApi('<your-plugin-id>', '1.3'); // minimum API version required
  // ...register capabilities...
  api.initializationComplete();
}
main();
```

- The `major.minor` you pass is the **minimum API version your plug-in needs from the deployed
  i2 Notebook backend** — *not* the version of the SDK you happened to install. The call asks the
  running server "do you serve a client that supports at least this API version?" and **rejects** if
  the server is older than requested (or if `pluginId` is absent from the manifest).
- **Choose the lowest version that includes every API you actually use.** A lower number runs on a
  wider range of i2 Analyze servers; a higher number requires a newer server but unlocks newer APIs.
  See the SDK ↔ i2 Analyze compatibility table in the *SDK and API versioning* guide.
- Ceiling: it can't exceed the API version of the installed `@i2analyze/notebook-sdk` (you can only
  call types the SDK ships). Within that ceiling, prefer the floor. The `create-notebook-plugin`
  scaffold sets a deliberately low default (currently `1.3`) for broad compatibility — only raise it
  when you adopt an API introduced in a later version. **Do not "upgrade" it to match the SDK.**
- (The templates use the unbundled global `notebook`, so you choose the version explicitly. If you
  instead `import { getEntryPointApi }` from the SDK and bundle it, that entry point uses the SDK's
  own version automatically.)
- Keep the `pluginId` identical in code and manifest.
- You **must** call `api.initializationComplete()` once setup is done, or the plug-in never finishes loading.

## 3. Commands (the primary way to add behaviour)

Create with `api.commands.createCommand({...})`, then *surface* it into one or more UI locations.
Command `type` scopes the execution context: `'unscoped'`, `'records'`, etc. The scaffold uses
`'unscoped'`; switch to `'records'` when you act on the current selection.

```ts
const cmd = api.commands.createCommand({
  id: 'view-on-map',
  name: 'View on map',
  icon: { type: 'inlineSvg', svg: commandSvg },
  type: 'records',
  onExecute(payload: commands.IRecordsContext) { /* ... */ },
  onSurface(action, eventApi, signal) {
    // Control enablement per surfacing. dispatchNow runs the callback immediately;
    // forwarding `signal` auto-unsubscribes when this surfacing is removed.
    eventApi.addEventListener('recordscontextchange',
      (ctx) => action.setEnabled(/* predicate over ctx.records */ true),
      { dispatchNow: true, signal });
  },
});

api.commands.applicationRibbon.homeTab.surfaceCommands(cmd);
api.commands.chartPopupMenu.surfaceCommands(cmd); // same command, multiple places
```

**Best practice:** gate enablement in `onSurface` via events rather than leaving buttons always-on;
always forward `signal` to listeners so they clean up on unsurface.

## 4. Reading data

Access via the versioned `data` / `records` / `chart` namespaces. Records expose typed properties
through their `itemType`.

- Iterate `record.itemType.propertyTypes`; read with `record.getProperty(propertyType)`.
- **Check `record.isValueUnfetched(property)` before use** — the client lazily loads values, and an
  unfetched value is not the same as an empty one. See guide: *Unfetched property values*.
- Collections are `data.IReadOnlyCollection<T>` (use `.size`, `.firstOrDefault(undefined)`), not JS arrays.

## 5. Changing data — tracked vs untracked mutations

All writes go through a mutation callback; never mutate model objects directly.

- **`runTrackedMutations`** — for changes that modify data (add/edit/delete records, notes, etc.).
  These are undoable and validated. Return `{ type: 'commit' }` or `{ type: 'rollback' }`.
- **`runUntrackedMutations`** — for view-only changes that don't touch data, e.g. selection or
  untracked element style. Lighter weight; not part of undo history.

```ts
await api.runTrackedMutations(async (application, mutations, cancelation) => {
  if (application.chart.selection.records.size === 0) return { type: 'rollback' }; // no-op, not an error
  const id = mutations.addEntityRecord({ itemType, properties: {}, notes: [], security, sourceReferences: [] });
  return { type: 'commit' };
});
```

Guides: *Changing data from a plug-in*, *Supported mutation operations*, *Untracked element style editing*.

## 6. Dev loop, build, deploy

- `npm run dev` — dev server + `notebook-sdk-plugin-proxy` (proxies to your i2 Analyze server; edit
  `devproxy.json` to change the target). Open the Web Client and look for your ribbon button /
  console message.
- `npm run build` — production webpack bundle into `dist/`.
- **Deploy:** copy `dist/` into the server's
  `toolkit/configuration/fragments/opal-services/plugins/<your-plugin>/`, then
  `setup -t stopLiberty && setup -t deployLiberty && setup -t startLiberty` (repeat on every Liberty
  node in HA). Guide: *Deploying to an i2 Analyze server*.

## 7. Versioned API namespaces

Import types from `@i2analyze/notebook-sdk`; the runtime API is grouped into:
`app`, `chart`, `commands`, `data`, `dialog`, `records`, `schema`, `toolview`, `visual`
(plus `ILogger`, `IEntryPointApi`, `LogLevel`). Prefer these typed namespaces over `any`.

## 8. Footguns / anti-patterns

- ❌ Hand-rolling the project or copying `basic-plugin` — see §0.
- ❌ Guessing the API version, or letting manifest `pluginId` drift from the code id.
- ❌ Forgetting `api.initializationComplete()`.
- ❌ Reading a property without an `isValueUnfetched` check.
- ❌ Using `runTrackedMutations` for selection-only changes (use untracked), or mutating model objects outside a mutation callback.
- ❌ Leaving commands always-enabled instead of gating in `onSurface`.
- ⚠️ Before relying on a member, check its `@i2since` tag in the API reference: it names the API
  version that introduced it. If you use it, the plug-in's requested minimum version (§2) must be at
  least that value. The public API is a single stable surface — there are no `@beta`/`@alpha` tiers.

## 9. When unsure

Prefer these accurate sources over memory: the API reference
(https://i2group.github.io/notebook-sdk/api/), the guide, the `samples/` directory, and
`packages/notebook-sdk/src/use-the-api.ts` (worked mutation examples). For machine ingestion, fetch
`https://i2group.github.io/notebook-sdk/llms-full.txt`.

<!-- END: Agent guide (AGENTS.md) -->

<!-- BEGIN: Welcome -->

# Welcome to the i2 Notebook SDK

The i2 Notebook SDK enables you to write _plug-ins_ that enhance and extend the functionality of the i2 Notebook web client.
For example, you might use a plug-in to add a new command to the application ribbon, or to provide a new tool for analyzing or displaying data in a way that's integrated with the rest of the i2 Notebook user interface.

The i2 Notebook web client exposes a JavaScript API that i2 Notebook plug-ins can target with JavaScript or TypeScript code.

For a plug-in that has a visual representation, you can write user interface code in HTML/CSS, or by using a framework such as Angular, React, or Vue.

**Note:** During development, if you want to use a third-party framework or our plug-in proxy, Node.js is required. When development is complete, plug-ins do not require Node.js in order to run.

The table of contents on the left includes conceptual and tutorial documentation for the i2 Notebook SDK:

- The topics that follow this introduction describe the structure of plug-ins for the i2 Notebook web client, and introduce some features of the SDK.

- The [Tutorials](guide/tutorials/tutorials.md) section contains worked examples of using the SDK to create i2 Notebook plug-ins.

You don't need to read the conceptual documentation before you follow the tutorials.
The conceptual documentation provides more information about subjects that the tutorials mention in passing. You can return to those topics when you create plug-ins of your own.

For an overview of what i2 Notebook plug-ins can do, see the [**Capabilities overview**](./guide/capabilities-overview.md).
For a more detailed account, use the [**Notebook API**](./api/index.md) tab at the top of the page to read the i2 Notebook API documentation.

<!-- END: Welcome -->

<!-- BEGIN: What's new in 1.10 -->

# What's new in version 1.10

Version 1.10 of the i2 Notebook API adds richer command groups, invocation context for commands,
appearance hints for new chart elements, badges, edge summary styling, hover events, read-only chart detection,
more flexible dialog sizing, and several new system commands.

- **Command invocation context** — Command handlers now receive the chart position and keyboard modifier state at the point at which the command was triggered, so that a plug-in can, for example, place a new node under the cursor.
- **Dynamic command groups** — Register groups whose commands are created each time the group opens, either synchronously or asynchronously.
- **Command group enhancements** — Groups gain an `onSurface` state hook, split-button primary commands, a `'stacked'` layout, ribbon-style pop-outs, and reusable group templates that you can surface into several places.
- **Appearance hints for new elements** — When you add a record in a tracked mutation, you can specify the color, label, size, position, and other appearance details of the element that the system creates for it.
- **Badges** — Read and set badge icons on nodes and edges.
- **Edge summary styling** — Read the style of an edge summary, and override its color, direction, line style, and width.
- **Hover events** — The new `charthoverchange` event fires when the pointer enters, leaves, or moves between chart elements.
- **Read-only charts** — Detect whether the user opened the chart as a read-only snapshot.
- **Dialog sizing** — Plug-in dialogs support an `'xmedium'` size, custom dimensions, and automatic height.

## Root API

`IEntryPointApi`

- [`pluginBaseUrl`](../api/notebook-sdk.ientrypointapi.pluginbaseurl.md) — the base URL from which the plug-in's assets are served. The URL always ends with a forward slash.

`NotebookStatic`

- [`getEntryPointApi`](../api/notebook-sdk.notebookstatic.getentrypointapi.md) accepts `'1.10'` as an `apiVersion`. The bundled `getEntryPointApi` function now requests version 1.10.

## app namespace

`ITrackedMutations`

- [`createNode`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.itrackedmutations.createnode.md) and [`createEdge`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.itrackedmutations.createedge.md) — after you add an entity or link record, pass the pending record to obtain an editor that hints the appearance of the element that the system creates for it. The element is created with the hints applied, rather than first appearing with its default appearance.

`IElementEditorBase`

- [`setBadge`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.ielementeditorbase.setbadge.md) and [`clearBadges`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.ielementeditorbase.clearbadges.md) — set or clear the badge icons on a node or edge.

`INodeEditor`

- The inherited setters (`setLabel`, `setBadge`, `clearBadges`) now return the node editor, so that you can chain them with node-specific setters such as `setCenter`, `setSize`, and `setImage` in any order.

`IEdgeSummaryEditor`

- [`setColor`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.iedgesummaryeditor.setcolor.md), [`setDirection`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.iedgesummaryeditor.setdirection.md), [`setLineStyle`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.iedgesummaryeditor.setlinestyle.md), and [`setWidth`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.iedgesummaryeditor.setwidth.md) — override the style of an edge summary.

## chart namespace

`IChart`

- [`isReadOnly`](../api/notebook-sdk.chart.ichart.isreadonly.md) — whether the user opened the chart as a read-only snapshot. On a read-only chart, mutations that would change the chart are rolled back, and their promises resolve with a result that contains no changes.

`ChartEventMap`

- [`charthoverchange`](../api/notebook-sdk.chart.charteventmap.charthoverchange.md) — new event that fires when the pointer enters, leaves, or moves between chart elements, but not on every pointer movement. The [`HoverChangeListener`](../api/notebook-sdk.chart.hoverchangelistener.md) receives the hovered node, edge, edge summary, or node group, or `null` when the pointer leaves all elements.

`IRecordChanges`

- [`direction`](../api/notebook-sdk.chart.irecordchanges.direction.md) — present and `true` for link records whose direction changed.

## commands namespace

`ICommandConfig`

- `onExecute` now receives an [`ICommandInvocationContext`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.icommandinvocationcontext.md), with `triggerPosition` and `modifierKeys` ([`IModifierKeys`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.imodifierkeys.md)), through the new [`CommandExecutePayloadMap`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.commandexecutepayloadmap.md). For `'unscoped'` commands, the context is an optional argument, so existing `onExecute` handlers that declare no parameter continue to work unchanged. An `'unscoped'` handler that explicitly declares a `void` parameter, such as `onExecute(_payload: void)`, no longer compiles; remove the parameter, or declare it as `invocationContext?: commands.ICommandInvocationContext`.

`ICommandApi`

- [`createGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.icommandapi.creategroup.md) — returns a detached [`IGroupTemplate`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.igrouptemplate.md) that you build once and surface into one or more action areas.

`IActionArea`

- [`addDynamicGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.iactionarea.adddynamicgroup.md) — add a group whose commands are created each time its host surface (pop-up menu or ribbon drop-down) opens. The group's `onPopulate` callback receives an [`IDynamicActionArea`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.idynamicactionarea.md), and can return a promise; the host opens the pop-up immediately with placeholder rows and shows the real items when the promise resolves.
- [`surfaceGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.iactionarea.surfacegroup.md) — surface a group template that was created with `createGroup`.
- `addGroup` and `addOrGetGroup` are now generic in the command type, so that the type of a group's `onSurface` event API is inferred from its `context`.

`IGroup` / `IDynamicGroupConfig`

- `IGroup` is now a union of [`IStandardGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.istandardgroup.md) and [`ICommandGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.icommandgroup.md), and `IDynamicGroupConfig` is a union of [`IStandardDynamicGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.istandarddynamicgroup.md) and [`ICommandDynamicGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.icommanddynamicgroup.md).
- `primaryCommand` — specifies a `'command'` (split-button) group's primary command, which runs when users click the main part of the button. If a static group does not specify one, the first command that is surfaced in the group is its primary command, as in version 1.9. A dynamic `'command'` group must specify one. No other group type can specify one.
- `onSurface` — drive a group's label, icon, and enabled or hidden state from application events through an [`IGroupAction`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.igroupaction.md), in the same way as `ICommandConfig.onSurface` for individual commands. Disabling an expanded group also disables its immediate children.
- `context` — selects the command context type for the group's `onSurface` event API. It is optional on static groups, where it defaults to `'unscoped'`. On dynamic groups it is required, and it also determines the payload that `onPopulate` receives.
- `popoutStyle` — on a static `'collapsed'` or `'command'` group, set to `'ribbon'` to open a floating ribbon-style panel instead of a standard drop-down menu.

`GroupType`

- [`'stacked'`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.grouptype.md) — displays a group's children as a vertical column of small buttons in the ribbon, which collapses under overflow pressure. In pop-up menus, the children are displayed as normal menu items below a section header.

`ISystemCommands`

- [`copyToNewChart`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.copytonewchart.md)
- [`getMatches`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.getmatches.md)
- [`renameChart`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.renamechart.md)
- [`shareChart`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.sharechart.md)
- [`toggleFindConnectingNetworks`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.togglefindconnectingnetworks.md)
- [`toggleSocialNetworkAnalysis`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.togglesocialnetworkanalysis.md)

Command, group, and ribbon tab identifiers no longer need to be GUIDs. Any non-empty string is accepted, although a GUID or other globally unique value is still recommended to avoid collisions with other plug-ins.

## dialog namespace

`IDialogConfig`

- `size` now accepts:
  - `'xmedium'` — a new preset [`DialogSize`](../api/notebook-sdk.dialog.dialogsize.md) between `'medium'` and `'large'`.
  - [`IDialogDimensions`](../api/notebook-sdk.dialog.idialogdimensions.md) — explicit CSS `width` and `height` lengths, each limited to the `'large'` size.
  - [`IDialogAutoHeightSize`](../api/notebook-sdk.dialog.idialogautoheightsize.md) — a preset `width` with `height: 'auto'`, which makes the dialog's height fit its content.

## schema namespace

`IChartPropertyType`

- [`itemType`](../api/notebook-sdk.schema.ichartpropertytype.itemtype.md) — the item type that owns the property type.

## visual namespace

`IElementStyleBase`

- [`badges`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ielementstylebase.badges.md) and [`getBadge`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ielementstylebase.getbadge.md) — the badge icons on a node or edge; see [`IBadgeIcon`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibadgeicon.md) and [`BadgeSlot`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.badgeslot.md).

`IEdge`

- [`summary`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.iedge.summary.md) — the edge summary that contains the edge, if any.

`IEdgeSummary`

- [`style`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.iedgesummary.style.md) — the style of the edge summary; see [`IEdgeSummaryStyle`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.iedgesummarystyle.md).

## Tooling

- The SDK packages are built with TypeScript 6. The public API is unchanged.
- The minimum supported Node.js version is now 20.19.
- The `@i2analyze/notebook-sdk` package and projects that `@i2analyze/create-notebook-plugin` generates now include an `AGENTS.md` file with guidance for AI coding assistants.
- The plug-in manifest supports an `isModule` field for plug-ins that are ES modules.

## Deprecations

- **`ISystemCommands.saveChart`**: Deprecated. The system now saves charts automatically. Use `renameChart` to rename a chart, or `shareChart` to manage sharing and access control.

<!-- END: What's new in 1.10 -->

<!-- BEGIN: What's new in 1.9 -->

# What's new in version 1.9

Version 1.9 of the i2 Notebook API adds support for brush sets, granular property-level change tracking in chart change events,
improved mutation APIs that return promises, new line and border styling options, local-only element style editing,
and several smaller additions and deprecations.

- **Brush Sets API** — Create and manage brush sets to apply color-based highlighting to chart elements with discrete or gradient color ranges.
- **Property-level change tracking** — Chart change events now include granular details about which properties, notes, and source references changed within each record.
- **Async mutations** — `runTrackedMutations` and `runUntrackedMutations` now return promises for better control flow in long-running operations.
- **Direct chart and view access** — Access the chart and view objects directly from the root API for simplified data queries and operations.
- **Line and border styling** — New `lineStyle` and `borderStyle` properties on nodes, edges, and groups with support for solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot, and dash-dot-dot styles.
- **Local-only style editing** — Edit element appearance locally without persisting changes to the server, useful for transient UI state.
- **Group layout commands** — New layout commands that work within groups or on selections.

## app namespace

`IApplication`

- [`brushSets`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.iapplication.brushsets.md) — access to the brush sets manager for creating and managing brush sets.
- [`valueFactory`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.iapplication.valuefactory.md) — factory for creating values used in the API, including brush color ranges.

`ITrackedMutations` / `IUntrackedMutations`

- `runTrackedMutations` and `runUntrackedMutations` now return a promise of the mutation response. The callback API is deprecated.
- [`setProgress`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.istatus.setprogress.md) — new mutation API for setting progress during long-running operations.
- `IUntrackedMutations` provides methods (`editNode`, `editEdge`, `editEdgeSummary`, `editNodeGroup`) for editing element appearance locally without persisting to the server. Useful for temporary styling, transient highlights, or UI state visualization. Changes are applied immediately to the chart UI but are lost on page reload.

`IValueFactory`

- [`createBrushColorRange`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.ivaluefactory.createbrushcolorrange.md) — create discrete or continuous (gradient) color ranges for brush sets.

`PropertiesSpecifier` / `EditPropertiesSpecifier`

- New common specifier types for record properties in mutation APIs.

`IApplicationContents`

- [`chart`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.iapplicationcontents.chart.md) and [`view`](../api/notebook-sdk.app.iapplicationcontents.view.md) — direct access to chart and view on root APIs.

## chart namespace

`IChartChangeMinor`

- [`recordChanges`](../api/notebook-sdk.chart.ichartchangeminor.recordchanges.md) — optional field providing granular change details for each changed record, enabling plug-ins to determine exactly which properties, notes, and source references changed.

`IRecordChanges`

- New interface providing detailed change information for properties, notes, and source references within records; see [`IRecordChanges`](../api/notebook-sdk.chart.irecordchanges.md).

`ChartEventMap`

- [`brushsetchange`](../api/notebook-sdk.chart.charteventmap.brushsetchange.md) — new event fired when a brush set changes.

## visual namespace

`INodeStyle` / `IEdgeStyle` / `INodeGroupStyle`

- [`lineStyle`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.iedgestyle.linestyle.md) — line style property added to edge visual styles.
- [`borderStyle`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.inodestyle.borderstyle.md) — border style property added to node and group visual styles.
- Added [`LineStyle`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.linestyle.md) type with support for `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `dash-dot`, and `dash-dot-dot` styles.
- Updated border color, border width and border style valid options.

`IBrushSet`

- [`id`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushset.id.md)
- [`isActive`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushset.isactive.md)
- [`colorRange`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushset.colorrange.md)
- [`setColorRange`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushset.setcolorrange.md)
- [`set`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushset.set.md) — set brush indices for records.
- [`remove`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushset.remove.md)
- [`getBrushIndex`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushset.getbrushindex.md)
- [`clear`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushset.clear.md)

`IBrushSetsManager`

- [`create`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushsetsmanager.create.md)
- [`activate`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushsetsmanager.activate.md)
- [`deactivate`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushsetsmanager.deactivate.md)

`IBrushColorRange`

- [`getColor`](../api/notebook-sdk.visual.ibrushcolorrange.getcolor.md) — resolve a brush index to a CSS color string, with interpolation for continuous ranges.

## commands namespace

`ISystemCommands`

- [`layoutGroupedOnSelection`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutgroupedonselection.md)
- [`layoutGroupedWithinGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutgroupedwithingroup.md)
- [`layoutPackedOnSelection`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutpackedonselection.md)
- [`layoutPackedWithinGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutpackedwithingroup.md)
- [`layoutPeacockOnSelection`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutpeacockonselection.md)
- [`layoutPeacockWithinGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutpeacockwithingroup.md)
- [`layoutCircularOnSelection`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutcircularonselection.md)
- [`layoutCircularWithinGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutcircularwithingroup.md)
- [`layoutOrganizationOnSelection`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutorganizationonselection.md)
- [`layoutOrganizationWithinGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutorganizationwithingroup.md)
- [`layoutMinimizeCrossedLinksOnSelection`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutminimizecrossedlinksonselection.md)
- [`layoutMinimizeCrossedLinksWithinGroup`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.isystemcommands.layoutminimizecrossedlinkswithingroup.md)

`IGroup`

- [`type`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.grouptype.md) — new property whose `GroupType` values are `'expanded'`, `'collapsed'`, or `'command'`; it supersedes the deprecated `isCollapsed` boolean. The `'command'` value creates split-ribbon-button command groups.

## schema namespace

`ChartItemTypeIdentifier`

- New type that allows schema types to be identified by either `ChartItemTypeId` or `AnalyzeItemTypeId`.

`PropertyTypeIdentifier`

- New type that allows record properties to be identified by either `ChartPropertyTypeId` or `AnalyzePropertyTypeId`.

## data namespace

`IBaseChartData`

- New base interface for common chart data properties; see [`IBaseChartData`](../api/notebook-sdk.data.ibasechartdata.md).

## Deprecations

- **Callback API for mutations**: The callback parameter on `runTrackedMutations` and `runUntrackedMutations` is deprecated. Use the returned promise instead.
- **`RecordPropertiesSpecifier` / `EditRecordPropertiesSpecifier`**: Deprecated in favor of `PropertiesSpecifier` and `EditPropertiesSpecifier`.
- **`IChartChangeMajor`**: The distinction between major and minor chart changes has been removed. All chart change events are now of type `'minor'`. Use `IChartChange` instead. This interface will be removed in the next major release.
- **`IGroupBase.isCollapsed`**: Deprecated in favor of `IGroup.type`.
- **`app.ThemeName` and `app.ITheme.themeName`**: Deprecated.

<!-- END: What's new in 1.9 -->

# What's new in version 1.8

Version 1.8 of the i2 Notebook API adds support for node groups (grouping nodes together on a chart),
expanded editing capabilities for node groups and edges, new system commands and ribbon areas for grouping and layouts,
and several small improvements to collection APIs and source-reference metadata.

<!-- BEGIN: What's new in 1.7 -->

# What's new in version 1.7

Version 1.7 of the i2 Notebook API enhances the customization options for the application ribbon, allowing the removal of existing ribbon tabs.
This allows the application ribbon UI to be fully customized, replacing the standard ribbon tabs with your own arrangement of tools and commands to fit your specific requirements.

The new version also adds a flag to the security dimension values of records to show when a value has been "suspended" due its removal from the current security schema.

## commands namespace

`IApplicationRibbon`

- [`removeTab`](../api/notebook-sdk.commands.iapplicationribbon.removetab.md)

## schema namespace

`ISecurityDimensionValue`

- [`suspended`](../api/notebook-sdk.schema.isecuritydimensionvalue.suspended.md)

<!-- END: What's new in 1.7 -->

# What's new in version 1.6

Version 1.6 of the i2 Notebook API adds the ability to create and edit custom types in the chart's schema.
The new version also allows plugins to extend the application ribbon with new ribbon tabs as a place to surface commands.
Finally, charts in i2 Notebook now support edge summarization, including the ability to set the labels of edge summaries to customize their appearance.

# What's new in version 1.5

Version 1.5 of the i2 Notebook API contains new functionality for modifying element labels and node images.
The new version also extends the API for command surfacing to allow group nesting behavior to be controlled and commands to be hidden and their icon dynamically updated.
